artifacts.summary: Maps the new dirty-worktree-vs-file_scope advisory onto the existing idle_overlap_advisory/absent_scope_advisory/cross_session_hazard pattern across orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, and orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh (Class J), reuses scopes_overlap_first() with no new jq logic, rules out any git-snapshot.sh code change, and flags the real gap: neither named regression suite's TMPROOT is an actual git repo today.

memory_candidates.content: In orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's jq program (lib/file-scope-overlap.sh's spliced FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS), scopes_overlap_first(own_scope; other_scope) can double as a containment predicate for a single concrete path by passing [path] (or an array of concrete paths) as other_scope -- exact match or directory-prefix-ancestor in either direction already answers 'is this concrete path covered by this declared scope', with no new jq def needed. One accepted blind spot: glob-shaped scope entries are invisible to it (Class G already warns about this elsewhere).

Additive, decision-never-changing advisory fields on an orchestrate-batch-admit.sh verdict follow one converged 4-surface pattern: (1) bash-layer precompute once per invocation with a degrade-safe default (e.g. sessions_json, critical_expanded_json), (2) a jq fragment computed once from the candidate's own file_scope/relevant inputs and merged (+ $frag) into every verdict branch the fold can produce, (3) a mirrored *_ledger field in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's mt_state_file (declared in header comment, //= [] initializer, capture block inside the per-row read loop keyed on 'field != null'), (4) a new lettered Class in orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh (next unused letter; a field that never changes decision gets ONE rendering block with no deferred/admitted split, unlike C/D/H which split because their signal can also cause a defer).

common_repo_root() (lib/common.sh) is pure path arithmetic -- it walks up N directory levels from the script's own location, never calling 'git rev-parse'. Consequently, test suites that build an isolated $TMPROOT by copying scripts byte-for-byte (test-conflict-predicate.sh, test-four-tier-conflict.sh) resolve a valid PROJECT_ROOT inside $TMPROOT even though $TMPROOT is never an actual git repository (no 'git init' in either suite). Any new check that shells out to real git commands (e.g. 'git diff --name-only HEAD') will silently degrade to empty/failure inside these existing fixtures unless the fixture builder is extended with git init + a baseline commit.
